findings.source_text: **COL-1 · Critical · VERIFIED (re-run independently) · `raven/slurm.py:1104-1131` (re-raise at `:1110-1113`); `platform_session.py:128-129`, `:140-141`; `raven_collection.py:36`; `slurm_json.py:27-28`, `:57-58`, `:75-79`.** Every installed launcher runs in managed mode, and on Slurm 23.02+ (whose `--help` advertises `--json`) Raven asks for `squeue --json` / `sacct --json` first. findings.source_text: **HV-3 · Critical · VERIFIED (re-checked independently) + salloc(1) · `raven/raven_worker_client.py:374-393`; `raven_allocation_helper.py:329-331`, `:340`, `:435`; `raven_allocation.py:562-585`; `raven_launch.py:173-175`.** Every Raven-initiated stop goes through `WorkerClient.close(timeout=1)`: Cancel, Release, idle or lease release, the pending timeout, quit, the startup deadline, and UI death or SSH hang-up (the UI has no SIGHUP handler, so the helper just sees EOF). `close()` writes a shutdown frame that a pending `salloc` never reads, waits one second, then sends `killpg(SIGKILL)`. Per salloc(1), only a catchable signal makes salloc revoke a PENDING request, so the queued job survives; a granted salloc killed before its relinquish completes never releases. With `InactiveLimit=0` (the upstream example value) the ownerless allocation runs to `--time` (1 h by default), billed, and Raven marks it reconciling but cannot clean it up (HV-1, HV-2; auto-cancel is limited to Slurm 26.05.5). Cancel while pending: the helper exited in 1.05 s, `salloc got a catchable signal (could revoke): False`, receipt `reconciling`, job 9001 left queued; quit and the pending timeout behave the same. A helper crash does better than a deliberate Cancel: PDEATHSIG delivers SIGTERM and salloc logs `revoked:15`. Over SSH the SIGKILL hits the local `ssh` client, and `ssh -T` has no PTY to carry a hang-up, so the remote salloc gets no signal at all (CODE-READ). Fix: while pending, SIGTERM salloc and wait at least MessageTimeout plus a margin (about 30 s); once granted, send the shutdown frame, wait briefly, then SIGHUP salloc and wait; SIGKILL only after a long bound; keep the job id and name in the receipt for a name-based `scancel`; make `--remote-launch` a supervising parent that turns stdin EOF or SIGHUP into a signal to salloc instead of exec'ing it.

findings.source_text: **ANA-1 · High · VERIFIED (re-run independently) · `raven/experiment_design.py:96-146`, `:158-161`, `:186-194`.** The factorial model fits main effects, two-way interactions and blocks, and checks only that this reduced matrix has full rank. With three or more factors, if any planned cell has no supported observation (all repetitions excluded or never run), the omitted three- and four-way interaction columns alias onto the fitted ones and Raven reports confident, wrong contrasts. Blocked 2^3 design, 4 reps, `y = 10 + 1.5a + 0.9abc + noise(0.05)`, cell (+,+,+) excluded: state `observed-associations`, **a = +1.159 \[1.074, 1.243\] against a true +3.000**, and b, c, a:b, a:c, b:c all ≈ −1.80 with intervals excluding 0 against true 0. Without noise every contrast is wrong (state `zero-residual-variance`); with balanced data the three-way effect silently inflates the residual. The OLS arithmetic itself matches numpy and SciPy exactly. Fix: fit the full factorial when degrees of freedom allow; return "incomplete design" with no effects when any planned cell lacks a supported observation; if a reduced model is kept, run a lack-of-fit F-test against cell means and withhold intervals when it fails.
